_comment: An EXAMPLE compliance rule set, for the consumer's rule engine in
app/compliance. Nothing in Vision OS references this file — the platform
does not know rules exist, and it must not.
ALIGNED TO config/policies/kitchen-safety.example.json. Every attribute named
below is one that policy actually asks the platform to observe. A rule
depending on an attribute nobody observes can never reach a verdict, and
RuleSet.unproducible_against() reports exactly that at startup rather than
leaving it as a permanent UNKNOWN.
WHY THE CONDITIONS LOOK NEUTRAL. 'head_covering != none' rather than
'wearing_hairnet == true'. The platform refuses to register an attribute
whose name encodes a verdict, so the observation is a neutral enum and the
judgment lives here — the one place in the system where a threshold is
allowed to mean something.
THE 'message' FIELDS ARE THE END-USER SENTENCE. 'Employee #2 is not wearing
a head covering' is assembled from a subject label and the message below. It
is not generated by a model, which is why a stored finding regenerates the
identical sentence six months later.
FACE COVERING IS A SEPARATE RULE, AND DELIBERATELY INFORMATIONAL. Earlier
versions of this file carried a note here explaining that no mask rule
existed, because the kitchen policy declared no face-covering attribute.
Policy 2.1.0 declares one, so the note is gone and the rule is below.
It is NOT a third condition on kitchen.person.ppe.v1, and that is the whole
point of it being separate. Conditions are evaluated with Kleene semantics
and no short-circuit, and ANY false condition makes the whole finding a
VIOLATION at that rule's severity. Fold an unmeasured attribute into the
validated two-condition PPE rule and it can raise a HIGH-severity violation
on the strength of evidence nobody has scored yet.
Separate and informational, it observes without accusing: findings accrue
with full provenance and evidence refs, the head/hand rule is untouched and
cannot regress, and when live CCTV has produced annotated faces the
severity can be raised - or the condition folded in - on measured numbers
rather than on hope. site.object.identity.v1 below is informational for a
closely related reason.

_require_comment: 'unknown_values' is what keeps a refusal from becoming a violation.
Both attributes carry 'not_visible' in their registered domain: the
model looked, the body part was inside a pot or out of frame, and it
said so. Without listing it here, 'not_visible' fails 'ne none' and
'eq gloves' exactly as a bare head or a bare hand would, and a person
nobody could actually see is reported as non-compliant.
Listed per condition rather than inferred, because only a rule author
knows which members of an enum are facts and which are refusals.

require.message: is not wearing a head covering

_comment: max_staleness_ms is STRICTER than the attribute's own validity. The
platform states when it stops vouching for a value; a rule may
additionally insist on something fresher before it will act, and the
stricter of the two wins.
Past this age the rule reports UNKNOWN — never COMPLIANT, and never
VIOLATION. A stale value is not evidence of either.
This is also what makes UNKNOWN observable in a demo: hand_covering
carries a 60s validity in the policy, so a subject that stops being
re-observed drifts into UNKNOWN rather than silently staying compliant.
Reads face_covering, declared by kitchen-safety policy 2.1.0. That
attribute costs no extra model call - it shares head_covering's crop -
so this rule is cheap to run and cheap to leave running while its
accuracy is still unmeasured.
=== WHY 'eq mask' AND NOT A LIST ===
The attribute's domain is none | mask | mask_below_nose | other |
not_visible. Only 'mask' satisfies this rule. The other two decided
values are treated as not-a-covering, and BOTH of those are judgments
this document is making rather than facts the platform reported:
mask_below_nose - a mask on the chin is a real, visible mask. The
observation says truthfully where it sits; this rule decides that
where it sits does not satisfy a nose-and-mouth requirement.
other - a face shield or a beard covering. Visibly present, visibly
not a mask over the nose and mouth. A deployment whose requirement
is satisfied by a shield changes this line to an 'in' operator and
changes nothing else, anywhere.
That split is the reason the enum carries five values instead of a
boolean. A model forced to answer yes-or-no about a chin mask has to
misreport what it can see; given a value for it, it reports the picture
accurately and this file carries the consequence.
=== NOT MEASURED ===
As of policy 2.1.0 no face has been annotated in this repository, so
this rule's precision and recall are UNKNOWN - not poor, unmeasured.
Phase 5 reached the same conclusion for head and hand and refused to
publish a violation metric. Do not raise this severity, and do not fold
it into the PPE rule, until real footage has been annotated and scored.

_unknown_comment: not_visible only. mask_below_nose and other are DECIDED states -
the model looked and reported what it saw - so they fail the
condition as they should. Listing them here would turn a seen
chin mask into 'we could not tell', which is the opposite of true.
require.message: is not wearing a mask over the nose and mouth

_comment: 90s, matching the PPE rule, against a 60s attribute validity. The
stricter of the two wins, so a face that stops being re-observed
drifts into UNKNOWN rather than staying quietly compliant.
No 'requires' key. That field means CORROBORATION and yields
EVIDENCE_UNVERIFIED when the Verification Policy withheld it -
correct for the identity rule below, wrong here. face_covering is
not governed by that policy, so naming it would park this rule in a
permanent unverified state.
Demonstrates PROTECTED EVALUATION. This rule concerns objects whose
identity a closed-set detector cannot settle on its own, and it declines
to conclude anything until the corroborating observation exists.
'requires' names visible_object_kind — the attribute the Verification
Policy governs. When the policy WITHHELD corroboration (because the
detector's claim was already good enough), this rule reports UNKNOWN
with reason EVIDENCE_UNVERIFIED rather than guessing. That is the
correct outcome, not a failure: the rule is saying it will not rule on
evidence it has declared insufficient.
The rule does NOT go and fetch corroboration. It cannot — the evaluator
holds no model, no crop path and no clock. Requesting evidence is the
Verification Policy's job, upstream, under budget.

require.message: could not be identified from the available image evidence
